description: The record types aidd knows: each with what it records and the schema of its `data`. A record is the agent's own account of something that happened, kept as history: never a person's yes, never evidence, and nothing reads it to stop a step. A type changes only by adding optional fields; a breaking change is a new type. aidd keeps and lists a record of a type it does not know, so an older aidd reads a newer one's records.

decision.description: A question a person answered: an ask before an action, a choice between options, or an open question. The agent records it after it acts on the answer.

action.description: The risk rule's action the question asked about, such as `git.push.force`. Required on an approval.

question.description: The question as the person saw it.

type.description: `approval`: yes or no to an action. `choice`: pick from `options`. `text`: an open question.

text.description: The exact words shown, never a summary, and never a secret's value.

options.description: On a choice only: the options shown.

multiple.description: On a choice only: whether the person may pick more than one option.

covers.description: What the yes applies to. A yes holds only for what the question showed.

outcome.description: `accept`: yes, or a pick. `decline`: no. `cancel`: the question was dismissed with no answer.

picked.description: On an accepted choice only: the ids of the options picked.

words.description: The person's exact reply, so "yes, but keep the summary" keeps its "but". Empty only on `cancel`.

by.description: Who answered, by their git name. `aidd records add` fills in `git config user.name` when it is left out; the MCP `record` tool never does, so there the agent names them.

delegate_answer.description: The delegate's answer to a delegated ask, written by the delegate's MCP `delegate_answer` tool after it ran the check again. An accept stands only while the check still passes. A defer is final for the action on that tree. aidd writes it itself, never `aidd records add` or the MCP `record` tool, and it is never a person's yes.

outcome.description: `accept`: the delegate said yes on a passing check. `defer`: the person decides.

reason.description: The delegate's reason, in one line.

check.description: The `delegate_check` record the answer's own check run wrote.

delegation.description: The default branch's commit whose config held the delegation.

delegate_check.description: One run of `aidd delegate check`: the action and what it covered, eligible or defer, and why. aidd writes it itself, never `aidd records add` or the MCP `record` tool. It is history: the check recomputes every gate each time and reads no record's claims, except a delegate's defer.

inputs.description: What the check read, such as the tip commit and the check run's id, for a person to read. Nothing reads it to decide.

report.description: An action at the `report` level: the agent took it on its own and said what it did.

action.description: The risk rule's action, such as `pr.open`.

said.description: What the agent told the person, in its words.

command.description: The command line, never with a secret's value in it.

paths.description: The paths, relative to the repository root.

head.description: The commit the action ran on.

tree.description: The head commit's tree, so an amend that keeps the tree keeps what the record covered.

base.description: The default branch's tip the action was checked against.

spec.description: The Spec a yes covers, such as an approval's.
